LESSON: WRITING 4.3.3 WRITING SYLLABLES (FA-FU, HA-HU)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.3: Writing 4.3.3 Writing Syllables (fa-fu, ha-hu)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 4.3.3 Writing Syllables (fa-fu, ha-hu), part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Which items bought from the market have syllable ‘ba’?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 4.3.3 Writing Syllables (fa-fu, ha-hu) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: interpretation and inference skills as learner joins sounds.

● Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learner writes syllables on a digital device.

Values:
● Unity: cooperation as learners collaborate in writing syllables on the board.

● Responsibility: persistence as learner writes syllables on the different writing surfaces without assistance.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Social cohesion as learner works collaboratively with others to write syllables on the board.

Link to other subjects:

learner relates the skill of writing sylabbles with all learning areas.
